subject: MeridianRx SLO sizing & deployment topology - confirmation
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@meridianrx.com>, Tom Willis <t.willis@meridianrx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: MeridianRx SLO sizing & deployment topology - confirmation

Hi Laura / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the clear rundown of the fraud-detection flow and the emergency case triage use case. Short recap of what we captured and the proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before we scope architecture and cost.

High-level pain points you described:
- Peak latency sensitivity for interactive triage: P95 generation latency target <= 300ms for 512-token prompts.
- Sustained throughput for batch lookups: steady 150 QPS inference traffic, with burst spikes up to ~350 QPS during morning churn.
- Cost/ops constraint: prefer reserved capacity for predictability, but need a fallback to hosted for spikes and DR.
- Data residency & audit: all inference logs and payloads must remain in us-west and be available for 90-day audit retention.

Model and feature preferences:
- You want to evaluate a 30B distilled variant first (lower cost) and compare quality against your current internal Llama-2-13B baseline.
- KV cache for long-lived context (patient history snippets) is a must.

Preliminary sizing and topology notes (attached matrix + topology PNG):
- Two-tier approach: Dedicated pool (8 GPUs p4d-equivalent) sized for steady-state 150 QPS at 512 tokens, with an autoscale burst group up to an additional 6 GPUs for spike coverage.
- Streaming + continuous batching to keep P95 under 300ms; target batch window 8–12ms for interactive path.
- Fallback routing: hosted model variant (smaller quantized 7B) for non-critical paths or if Dedicated utilization > 85%.

Action items / asks from your side:
1) Confirm target P95 and 99 numbers for both interactive triage and batch lookup flows (I captured 300ms P95; please confirm).
2) Share a representative sample of request size distribution (tokens per request) and hourly traffic profile for last 7 days.
3) Legal procurement: we’ll need to know if MeridianRx requires a custom DPA and a SOC2 attestation before kickoff.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Marissa will prepare a conservative sizing worksheet and a cost delta for distilled 30B vs quantized 13B by Tuesday (attached as meridianrx-slo-matrix.xlsx).
- I’ll draft a topology sketch with failover routing policies and KV cache placement (see redwood-deploy-topology.png).
- If we agree on sizing, we can run a 2-week POC on Dedicated + hosted fallback to validate latency/SLOs and cost.

Proposed checkpoint: Tue Apr 20, 10:00am PT — 30-minute sync to review sizing and a mutual action plan. Please confirm if that works.

Thanks — Sergio

--

Thanks Sergio — this is great and aligns with our notes. A couple of clarifications below.

Confirmed SLOs:
- Interactive triage: P95 <= 300ms, P99 <= 750ms for up to 512 tokens.
- Batch lookup (non-interactive API): average latency < 800ms; we allow higher P99 ~2s for large analytic requests.

Traffic profile (rough):
- Steady-state: 130–160 QPS between 10am–4pm PT.
- Morning spike: 7am–9am PT daily, short bursts, peak ~340 QPS.
- Night batch jobs: 00:00–02:00 PT, ~50 QPS but heavy token counts (avg 1,200 tokens).

Model preference: start with distilled 30B OR a quantized 70B candidate if you think it gives a clear accuracy win. We'll accept a 10% latency uplift for a significant quality boost.

Procurement: legal flagged that SOC2 Type II is required; they will send our standard DPA. We can share a PO if cost looks predictable after the sizing.

We can confirm Tue Apr 20 10:00am PT. Please add Tom to the sizing call (he’s our infra lead).

Thanks,
Laura

Appreciate the clarifications — noted P99 targets and the nightly heavy-token batch. Two quick follow-ups before Tue:

1) Token distribution sample: Laura, if you can drop a CSV with percentile token lengths (p50/p90/p99) for both interactive and batch jobs into the Drive folder linked above that would be ideal. That will let us tune KV cache size and batching windows.

2) Marissa / Karthik — looping you both in. High-level asks for engineering sizing:
   - Marissa: can you prepare two cost/latency curves for the following configs by Monday EOD?
   a) Dedicated pool (8x p4d equiv) + 6 GPU burst group, running distilled 30B (float16 where possible).
   b) Dedicated pool (same) + automatic fallback to hosted quantized 7B for non-interactive paths.
   Include token cost breakdown, expected P95/P99 from our internal microbenchmarks, and expected KV cache hit improvement with a 24-hour prefix cache.
   - Karthik: please surface any topology caveats for audit retention (90-day logs) and whether a private VPC deployment with a customer-managed KMS is necessary to satisfy MeridianRx legal. If private is required, estimate additional setup lead time (days).

Attachments: I attached the initial sizing matrix and topology sketch to help — feel free to edit in Drive.

I'll schedule the Tue 10:00am PT meeting and send a calendar invite with the Drive links.

Sergio
